heroText: Uppsala works best as a base in Sweden when you anchor days around Uppsala Cathedral, Uppsala University and Gamla Uppsala. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Stockholm-Arlanda Airport (ARN) handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.text: In 1160, King Eric Jedvardsson was attacked and killed outside the church of Östra Aros, and later became venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church.

In 1274, Östra Aros overtook Gamla Uppsala as the main regional centre, and when the cathedral of Gamla Uppsala burnt down, the archbishopric and the relics of Saint Eric were moved to Östra Aros, where the present-day Uppsala Cathedral was erected; it was inaugurated in 1435.

The city is the site of the oldest university in Scandinavia, founded in 1477, and is where Carl Linnaeus, one of the renowned scholars of Uppsala University, lived for many years; both his house and garden can still be visited.

history.label: 16th century
history.text: Uppsala is also the site of the 16th-century Uppsala Castle.
The city was severely damaged by a fire in 1702.
In ecclesiastical terms, the place has always belonged to Uppsala parish, from 1961 called Uppsala cathedral parish.
Until 1971, the town was part of the district court for Uppsala City Hall Court and has been part of the Uppsala Court since 1971.
After parish break-up in 1974, parts of the town are located in Gottsunda parish.
The arms bearing the lion can be traced to 1737 and have been modernised several times, most recently in 1986.
After further building expansion, some are also in Denmark-Funbo parish, before 2010 in Denmark parish.
